Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the StratoForge Industries Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up can be found by pressing * then 1 on your telephone keypad. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to StratoForge Industries' Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are David Hargrove, Chief Executive Officer; John Harlan, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Lawson, Chief Operating Officer; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; Emily Chen, Chief Strategy Officer; and Tom Reilly, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-K and 10-Q, for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those statements.

David Hargrove:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. StratoForge Industries delivered a solid performance in Q3 FY2024, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio across commercial aerospace, defense, and services. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering long-term value to our shareholders. Today, we'll discuss our revenue performance across key segments, investments in R&D for next-generation platforms, margin dynamics and net income results, growth in our service offerings and customer diversification, the drivers and challenges behind our top-line results, the geopolitical influences shaping defense spending, and the margins and cost performance on our major programs.

We are particularly excited about the recent advancements in our next-generation Collaborative Combat Aircraft program and its potential to drive decision superiority and future growth in unmanned systems. We are seeing strong demand for our defense systems, including hypersonic boosters and F-35 components, and our commercial aerospace business is recovering steadily with ramps in GTF and LEAP engine deliveries.

John Harlan:
Thank you, David. Now, let's turn to the financials. In Q3 FY2024, we reported revenue of $8.7 billion, representing a 9% increase year-over-year, or 11% on an organic basis excluding foreign exchange headwinds. Our GAAP earnings per share were $2.85, up 28% from the prior year. We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with $5.2 billion in cash and equivalents. Our guidance for the full year remains unchanged at $34.5-35 billion in revenue, with adjusted EPS of $11.50 to $12.00. We are actively managing our costs and investing in key growth initiatives like additive manufacturing and supply chain reshoring. We are also focused on returning capital to shareholders through our dividend, which we recently increased by 12%, and $500 million in share repurchases year-to-date.

Let me break down our performance starting with revenue by segment: commercial aerospace, defense, and services. Our Commercial Aerospace segment generated $4.1 billion, up 14% year-over-year and representing 47% of total revenues. This strong growth exceeded our guidance, driven by a 12% rise in OEM deliveries to 285 widebody and narrowbody engine and nacelle units, mainly for Boeing 787 Dreamliner and Airbus A320neo programs. The ramp-up of our geared turbofan production for the PW1100G variant was a highlight, with a record 65 modules shipped, up 25% from last year. Supply chain improvements, including resolution of titanium forging issues, boosted our book-to-bill to 1.3x and expanded backlog to over $52 billion, featuring major orders from Delta Air Lines and LATAM for LEAP-1A/1B cores. North America drove 55% of growth via U.S. fleet modernizations, Asia-Pacific 30% from IndiGo's A320neo push and COMAC C919 progress where we supply nacelles, while Europe grew 8% softer due to Ryanair delays but poised for Q4 upside with Airbus hitting 75 aircraft monthly. We're committing $450 million to SAF certification for GTF by 2026, aligning with ICAO net-zero targets, and margins rose 220 basis points to 18.2% on high-thrust mix and pricing amid inflation.

Defense revenues came in at $3.2 billion, up 4% organically and 37% of total. Demand held firm from U.S. DoD supplemental funding and ally buys amid Ukraine and Indo-Pacific tensions. Missile systems hit $1.1 billion, up 9%, with full-rate production on our hypersonic glide vehicle booster for the AGM-183A ARRW, delivering 18 units under a $4.2 billion ceiling, plus JASSM-ER ramps for Australia and Poland FMS. F-35 propulsion components added $850 million, up 6%, as Lockheed accelerated Lot 15/16. U.S. grew 5% on the $886 billion FY2024 NDAA, international 3% with Middle East up 12% on Patriot GEM-T for Saudi and UAE; Europe flat on Tornado retirements but upside from Sky Shield. Book-to-bill at 1.1x, backlog $48 billion including $2.3 billion IDIQ for CCA autonomy. Margins up 80 bps to 15.4% via fixed-price gains and lower R&D on NGAD demos. Forward focus includes $300 million on directed energy lasers.

Services rounded out at $1.4 billion, up 16% YoY and 16% of total, highlighting annuity-like margins. Fleet utilization hit 92% on 28,000 engines/structures, up from 87%, with post-pandemic travel and aging fleets boosting MRO 18%—$650 million commercial overhauls at full-capacity LEAP/CFM56 shops in San Antonio/Singapore, $450 million defense including F-35 parts under PBL. Our StratoPredict AI platform cut unplanned downtime 22% for United Airlines, enabling 10% pricing and repeat wins. Asia-Pacific led +22% via ANA/AirAsia, EMEA +14% on Lufthansa alliances. Margins peaked at 28.6%, up 310 bps, from productivity and 65% total-care mix. Overall backlog $112 billion, up 8%, book-to-bill 1.2x. Q4 guide: Commercial +12-15%, Defense +3-6%, Services +14-17%.

Specific financial highlights include gross margin of 23.8%, up 210 basis points year-over-year to the highest Q3 in five years, ahead of our 22.5-23.5% guide. This stemmed from program mix, with F-35 Lot 15 LRIP ramp adding 150 bps via matured learning curves and supply stability. Cost-outs like digital twins and MBSE slashed non-recurring engineering 18%, additive manufacturing on JASSM-ER cut waste 25%, and $120 million procurement savings on metals amid titanium stabilization. U.S. sales drove core gains, international up 100 bps to 22.1% on FMS to Poland HIMARS; Middle East pressured slightly by R&D amortization on Iron Dome. Sequentially, up 80 bps despite overhead on NGAD composites ramp.

Operating margin reached 14.2%, up 190 bps YoY and 70 bps sequentially—strongest since 2019 commercial peak. SG&A fell to 6.1% of sales, down from 6.8%, a $95 million cut via headcount optimization and AI automation, compliant with CAS 418. R&D at $452 million or 5.2%, up 8%, with 35% capitalized on hypersonics and Orion Artemis work. Space op margins hit 16.5% on Vulcan efficiencies. Minor commercial aftermarket hit from 737 MAX inventory contained to 20 bps. Full-year ops guide 14-15%.

Net income was $1.05 billion GAAP, $2.85 diluted EPS, up 28% and beating consensus $0.15; non-GAAP $1.12 billion, $3.04 EPS excluding pension/tax items. Tax at 20.8% via FDII on exports like Patriot to Germany/Japan. Interest $80 million up slightly, but refinanced to save $40 million annually. Pension 105% funded. Free cash flow $1.4 billion.

On revenue drivers and headwinds, drivers made up 85% of 15% growth equivalent here—wait, adjusting for our 9%—led by defense electronics/missiles up 22% to $4.2 billion on HGX-400 hypersonic ramps, $2.8 billion NDAA funding from Red Sea/Ukraine validations, PAC-3 MSE +28% with $650 million NATO exports, international mix to 32%. F-35 $1.9 billion +12% on Lot 15/16 avionics at 98% delivery via digital thread. Commercial $2.1 billion +9% on LEAP/GTF MRO +18%, 737 MAX/A320neo build rates to 52/month, widebody $450 million Delta/Emirates. Space $1.2 billion +30% on Victorious-7 NRO constellation $800 million IDIQ, PWSA laser comms, Japan $1.1 billion hypersonic sensors. Tech boosts: $250 million additive for blades, AeroPredict attach 65%, C4ISR for TITAN $900 million.

Headwinds capped organic at 12%: supply disruptions, metals inflation $180 million (aluminum +15%, titanium +22%), semis delaying radars $250 million—mitigated 60% via offtakes, dual-source TSMC. NGAD delays shifted $300 million H2, 737 MAX rework idled 15%, competition in UAVs prompted $150 million IRAD Vantage-X. Europe flat on German budgets, FX shaved 2%, labor premiums 12%. But Fortress Supply Chain targets 95% onshoring by 2026.

Program margins averaged 11.2%, up 150 bps YoY, sixth straight expansion quarter. Defense Systems 12.8% +220 bps, NextGen Strike Fighter Lot 14 +300 bps, EAC -$450 million, CPI 1.05/SPI 1.02 via digital twins. Hypersonics 14.5% on $2.1 billion FFP Indo-Pacific. Reserves released $120 million, inflation offset by 15% savings AI maintenance. Commercial 9.5% steady, EfficientWing 900 +2% growth vs EAC, 98% yield robotics. Space 13.1% +180 bps, Vulcan reusability -$300 million underrun, SDA Tranche 2 AM RF. Portfolio CPI 1.03, 65% FFP/CPIF backlog $128 billion. Full-year 11.0-11.5%.

Mike Lawson:
Thank you, John. Operationally, we have seen significant improvements in our supply chain management, allowing us to increase production rates on key programs like GTF modules and F-35 sustainment. We are also investing in automation and digital technologies to improve efficiency and reduce costs. Specifically, our new San Antonio MRO facility adds 35% capacity for F-35/F-16, servicing 120 airframes at 14% EBITDA, $250 million annualized. AeroPredict AI on 2,500 platforms cuts unscheduled events 22%, $180 million savings for DoD. Digital twins for hypersonics TRL 7, 40% test cuts in $2.8 billion LRHW sustainment. LogiTech acquisition secures $4.2 billion PBL backlog at 12-15% margins. Customer base grew to 185 primes, backlog $52.3 billion +21% YoY. U.S. 18% KC-46 MRO $900 million; Europe F-35 hub Italy $1.1 billion Poland/Romania; Asia +45% MQ-9 Japan $650 million, AUKUS $420 million, Indonesia/Philippines ScanEagle; Middle East THAAD/F-15 $750 million. Services now 55% EBITDA, targeting 35% mix by 2026, adjacencies space/CUAS SkyShield.

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thank you, Mike. On the technology front, we're making significant strides in next-generation propulsion and platforms, anticipating a competitive edge. Our Q3 R&D spend hit $452 million, up 15% YoY to 11.2% of revenue; full-year $1.82 billion or 12%, above peers' 8-10%, aligned with DoD $850 billion NDS amid China J-20/hypersonics, Russia Kinzhal.

NGAD platforms 40% allocation ~$728 million: $320 million CCA drones to TRL 8 by 2025, $150 million AFRL follow-on OMS Pengate; VCEs +30% efficiency $85 million hot-section beats. NGAD EMD FY26 $20 billion, AUKUS/NATO Tempest FCAS €10 billion.

Hypersonics 20% ~$364 million: HGV booster Mach 5+ plasma $180 million Q3, ARRW heritage, scramjets CMCs $120 million IRAD; HACM/LRSO teaming, DoD $4.7 billion FY25, Indo-Pacific A2/AD $5 billion FMS.

Space 25% ~$455 million: PWSA 120-sat LEO OISLs 100 Gbps 99.9% uptime $115 million Q3, quantum encryption JADC2; SDA/NRO CRADAs $200 million, VLEO $18 billion, UK ISTARI £2 billion, UAE buses.

Digital 15% ~$273 million: AI/ML swarms 95% success $90 million, cyber zero-trust, DARPA ANCILLARY $60 million B&P; DoD $1.8 billion AI, DO-178C Level A.

60% customer-funded de-risks $52 billion pipeline NGAD $25B/PWSA $15B/hypersonics $12B; ROIC 18-24 months tech, 5-7 years LRIP. U.S. DoD 75%, exports 20%; Ukraine/Taiwan boost. Fuels 15-20% growth vs 5% CAGR.

Emily Chen:
Thank you, Raj. From a strategic perspective, we are actively evaluating acquisitions to complement our portfolio and expand reach, like LogiTech for logistics. New models capture sustainment shift, services 40% sector revenues per SIPRI $2.2 trillion. Geopolitics drives: SIPRI $2.44 trillion 2023 +6.8%, 5-7% CAGR to 2028 $150-200 billion incremental, missiles/UAVs/5th-gen 40%.

Europe Ukraine: 23/32 NATO 2% GDP, Poland 4.1% F-35/HIMARS $12.4 billion backlog, EU €800 billion Compass/€8 billion EDF Arrow-4 Mach 9.

Middle East +12% $220 billion: Israel 5,000 Iron Dome/David's Sling $450 million Q2, Saudi/UAE THAAD/F-15EX 22% GCC share, Iran proxies $50 billion, HAWC LRIP.

Indo-Pacific: NDAA $886 billion/$28 billion PDI, AUKUS AUD 368 billion SSN, Japan $320 billion F-35B/GCAP sensors $8.7 billion F-35, Switchblade/JASSM 15-20% APAC growth.

U.S. supplementals $61 billion Ukraine/$14 billion Israel +14% gov revenue $4.2 billion, Replicator 1,000 drones/NGAD $250 million capex ISR 25% margins.

Backlog $45 billion 3.5x, 60% FMS, exports 32% +500 bps, dual-source GaN. FY24 guide $28.5-29.5 billion revenue 11.2-11.5% margins.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Instructions for queuing: press * then 1. Our first question comes from Josh Altman with Citi. Please go ahead.

Josh Altman:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the supply chain improvements and their impact on program execution?

David Hargrove:
Certainly, Josh. We've made targeted progress resolving titanium and semiconductor bottlenecks through dual-sourcing and long-term offtakes, achieving 60% mitigation on inflation variances and cutting lead times toward 12 weeks. This has enabled 98% on-time F-35 deliveries, 25% waste reduction via additive on missiles, and full-capacity MRO shops, directly supporting EAC underruns and margin expansion as John detailed. We're on track for 95% onshorability by 2026.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez:
Hi, thanks. I'm curious about the outlook for commercial aerospace recovery and any pricing power there?

John Harlan:
Maria, great question. Commercial outlook remains solid with +12-15% Q4 growth guide, backed by $52 billion backlog and 1.3x book-to-bill. Air traffic at 105% 2019 RPKs drives LEAP/GTF ramps, A320neo/737 MAX to 52/month, plus widebody modernization. Pricing discipline amid inflation, plus 10% uplift from digital services, supports 18.2% margins expanding further with SAF investments. Supply normalization offsets prior headwinds like MAX rework.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Peter Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Peter Kim:
Regarding the R&D investments and expected returns timeline?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Peter, our $1.82 billion FY24 R&D, 12% of sales, is disciplined with 60% customer-funded de-risking $52 billion bids. Returns start 18-24 months on tech transitions like CCA TRL 8, hypersonic plasma, space OISLs; 5-7 years LRIP like NGAD EMD $20 billion. Geopolitical tailwinds accelerate, positioning for 15-20% growth in $1 trillion A&D market.

David Hargrove:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on our strategic priorities, operational excellence, and innovation across hypersonics, NGAD, space resilience, and sustainable commercial platforms.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our Q3 FY2024 earnings call. A replay will be available on our investor relations website.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
